name: The Stettauer household at 2026 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_stettauer_mrs_d

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 2026 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 2026 Mrs. D. Stettauer & dr.; Charles S. Stettauer.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 2026, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The one live-in servant it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 is on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. Left off: David Stettauer (written "in Europe"; by 1904 the Blue Book lists Mrs. D. Stettauer). The 1910 census was not read. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Miss Stettauer
persons.note: The Blue Book prints '& dr.' after the household's name: an unmarried daughter at home, not named. 'Miss Stettauer' is the book's own form of address, not a recorded name.

persons.name: Charles S. Stettauer
persons.note: A son is read from the shared surname under the head's listing; the Blue Book does not state the relationship. The 1900 census lists Charles Stettauer here with the other columns left blank (ED 40, sheet 9A, line 17, leaf n810).

persons.name: Charles Rolde

born.note: The census gives April 1862, age 38 on 1 June 1900.

occupation.note: Written as "Coachman" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the rear building behind the house, as the head of his own household there (coachman); born April 1862, in Germany, married. Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904. Part of the name is hard to read on the sheet; this is the best reading.
